summary: A local news feature on entrepreneurs in a town who are investing in community development through philanthropy, a trend that grew after September 1, 2023. It profiles Jessica Munroe, Drs. Harold Jones and Lana Kensington, Oliver Brandt, Sandra Little and River Thompson, whose programs span technology, health, the environment, food and the arts. It backs their impact with figures from LEF and LEI studies and argues that business success should be measured beyond revenue.
one_line: Profiles of local entrepreneurs whose philanthropic programs in tech, health, environment, food and arts measurably benefit their community.
key_facts: A Local Entrepreneurs Foundation (LEF) study dated November 5, 2023 found 75% of surveyed entrepreneurs engaged in some philanthropy in the past year, 45% did monthly community service, and 30% set up charitable foundations or scholarship programs.
Jessica Munroe founded the nonprofit "Tech for Futures" from her tech startup Munroe Dynamics; it launched December 12, 2023 to bridge the digital divide.
Tech for Futures has outfitted three schools with computer labs, plans to double that by the end of the next fiscal year, and saw a 40% increase in students' computer literacy at benefitting schools.
The Local Economic Influence (LEI) report, released February 20, 2024, found a 20% increase in small business growth in neighborhoods where "Tech for Future" programs were introduced.

Dr. Harold Jones and Dr. Lana Kensington, owners of a private health clinic, began their Health Cluster approach on March 17, 2024, setting up two Clusters with a 15% decrease in common preventable illnesses in those zones.
Oliver Brandt, CEO of renewable energy firm Green Skies, created the annual "Green Skies Sustainable Grant", which funded 25 local businesses with $10,000 each as of April 7, 2024.
Businesses in Brandt's grant program saw a 10% reduction in carbon footprint within the first six months.
Sandra Little, owner of Little's Organic Farm, started "Feeding the Future" on May 5, 2024, supplying fresh produce to schools and food banks.
After five months, Feeding the Future raised fresh food availability by 50% in participating organizations and cut food insecurity in targeted school districts by 22%.
River Thompson, a restaurateur, created "Artisan's Trust" on August 18, 2024, which has put over $200,000 into local arts and culture.
Artisan's Trust has funded seven community art installations and two local theater productions, raising cultural engagement by 30%.
The article says the entrepreneurs are driven by civic duty and the view that a flourishing community benefits everyone, and that success extends beyond revenue.
